claims.evidence: When everything is on the list nothing feels urgent; there is no differentiation between quick tasks and time-consuming projects, so easy tasks get done first.
To-do lists assume an infinite amount of time and encourage you to keep adding tasks.
To-do lists are an organizational technique, not a productivity system; they track tasks but don't drive completion.
When we feel overwhelmed we go into fight/flight/freeze; the fix is to triage the most important tasks.
Task paralysis is the can't-start freeze: you want to begin and still cannot make the first move.
Overwhelm is a state where too much lands at once and the system shuts down rather than picking a lane.
Break tasks into smaller manageable chunks and limit focus to the two or three things that matter tomorrow.

claims.claim: Long, uncategorized to-do lists cause decision paralysis and emotional freeze.
claims.evidence: Too many tasks gives me decision paralysis so I number my to-do list and roll a 20-sided dice for which one to do.
claims.product_implication: Provide a randomized task selection mechanism for paralysis moments.

claims.claim: Traditional productivity apps fail because they accumulate tasks and become overwhelming.
claims.evidence: I've used every app; Tick Tick, Things, Workflowy etc, but I stop using them after a while as my to do lists are always overwhelming.
claims.product_implication: Do not build another feature-rich backlog manager; constrain list size.

claims.claim: Users switch to default iPhone notes or paper to avoid app feature clutter.
claims.evidence: Task management apps are good for what they do, but they are not todo lists... friction-y mess with way too many features.
claims.product_implication: Keep interface extremely simple and low friction.

claims.claim: Focusing on one single 'must-do' reduces stress and increases productivity.
claims.evidence: Focusing on one 'must-do' is way less overwhelming, and somehow I get more done!
claims.product_implication: Design core workflow to surface only 1 main task on screen.

claims.claim: Separating primary must-dos from secondary tasks prevents daily list overwhelm.
claims.evidence: Focus on the real must-dos and put other things on a secondary list.
claims.product_implication: Implement a 2-tier storage system: Active 1-3 Must-Dos vs Secondary Backlog.
